item.research_question: To determine the influence of Y2O3 nanoparticles on the microstructure, mechanical, and tribological properties of CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloys and explore their potential for wear-resistant materials.
item.material_system: CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy matrix reinforced with 0, 0.25 wt %, and 0.5 wt % Y2O3 nanoparticles (marked as 0-YOHEA, 0.25-YOHEA, 0.5-YOHEA)
item.processing_route: Mechanical alloying of equiatomic elemental powders (Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni) and Y2O3 nanoparticles in a planetary ball mill for 50 h at 300 rpm under Ar atmosphere, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 900 °C for 5 min under 50 MPa uniaxial pressure in a vacuum of 1 × 10−3 Pa
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile testing (strain rate 1 × 10−3·s−1), Vickers microhardness (1 N load for 15 s), and sliding wear tests (5 N load, 6 mm/s speed, 6 mm distance, 900 s duration, 25 ± 2 °C) against a GCr15 ball (9.525 mm diameter, 766 HV)
key_findings: The addition of 0.25 wt % Y2O3 increased the room temperature tensile strength from 868 MPa to 1001 MPa (a 15.2% increase) and increased elongation from 5.4% to 6.1%.
The addition of 0.5 wt % Y2O3 resulted in decreased tensile strength and elongation compared to the base alloy and the 0.25 wt % composite.
Microhardness increased from 276 HV (0 wt %) to 403 HV (0.25 wt %) but decreased to 311 HV (0.5 wt %).
The average grain size of the sintered composites decreased with increasing Y2O3 content: 210 ± 50.1 nm (0 wt %), 52 ± 23.2 nm (0.25 wt %), and 31 ± 11.6 nm (0.5 wt %).
The coefficient of friction remained similar across all samples, but the 0.25 wt % Y2O3 composite exhibited the lowest wear loss.
The 0.5 wt % Y2O3 composite showed the highest wear loss and deeper furrows on the worn surface compared to the other samples.
Y2O3 nanoparticles maintained a spherical shape with diameters of approximately 40 nm and 20 nm in the 0.25 wt % and 0.5 wt % composites, respectively.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the strengthening in the 0.25 wt % composite to three mechanisms: grain boundary strengthening (Hall-Petch relation), dispersion strengthening (Orowan looping where dislocations bow around particles), and load transfer from the soft matrix to hard particles. The decrease in properties at 0.5 wt % is attributed to the inverse Hall-Petch effect (softening in nanocrystalline structures) and complicated reasons not fully explained. Wear resistance is attributed to the formation of an oxide layer acting as a solid lubricant and the abrasive nature of Y2O3 particles at higher concentrations.
item.limitations: The authors state there is no good explanation for the softening observed in the 0.5 wt % Y2O3 composite despite the fine grain size, noting it may be due to 'complicated reasons'. They also note that the density of the samples showed a decreasing trend compared to theoretical density, though no obvious pores were found in optical images.
quotes: The addition of 0.25 wt % Y2O3 increased the room temperature tensile strength of the CrMnFeCoNi base from 868 MPa to 1001 MPa
The material surface produces an oxide layer that prevents direct contact between the steel ball and the alloy, resulting in a lower friction shear strength
